MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  APRIL 19, 2021

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 6:01 p.m. in George F Canyon Nature Center (Deck Area), 27305 Palos
  Verdes Drive East, Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR POPE.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR POPE led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Bain, Ciarolla, Persichina, Pope, Retz, Romanelli

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  McCormick

  STAFF PRESENT:  Michael Goldsmith, Maintenance Superintendent
  Cynthia Morquecho, Comm. Services Supervisor
  Daniel A-Haja, Community Services Coordinator

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  MARCH 15, 2021

  CHAIR POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF MARCH
  15, 2021.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  RECREATION FEE REVIEW

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a brief review of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA, TO
  APPOVE STAFF RECOMMENDATION AS FOLLOWS:

  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY’S
  RECREATION FEES AS RECOMMENDED BY STAFF.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  1
APRIL 19, 2021
   AYES:  Pope, Ciarolla, Bain, Persichina, Retz, Romanelli

  NOES:

  ABSENT:  McCormick

  The motion carries.

  7.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted overgrowth that was taken care of by Bennett
  Landscape at Rockbluff Park. Some three-rail fencing was flattened in the park and a sign
  needs to be replaced. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith will have staff look into the
  matter.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if neighbors have complained about the missing fencing.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted they were happy that the eyesore was
  gone. COMMISSIONER BAIN further reported that Highridge park was quite active over
  the weekend and masks were worn appropriately. Community Services Supervisor
  Morquecho added that the City’s planning department has approved a film permit for May
  4, 2021 and filming will take place at Highridge Park. COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the
  bushes would have to be cleared near the proposed mural area for the proposed art
  project. Community Services Supervisor Morquecho responded that staff will meet with
  the artist in July for an update.

  B.  HILLS ARE ALIVE SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted the August 7 date for the event and the expectation
  to hold a virtual option for the race. Staff is also considering running the race without a
  race director again this year. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI added that staff should look
  into other races such as Conquer the Bridge and other cities to see how they plan to
  conduct in-person races. He asked if the past race director was notified of the upcoming
  change. Community Services Supervisor Morquecho responded that MPH Productions
  was notified. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated this was a good year to implement a
  staff-run race. COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA suggested looking into Manhattan
  Beach’s 5k race for guidance as well. CHAIR POPE noted YMCA’s October stair race
  was moved to the Los Angeles Coliseum.

  C.  CHANDLER PARK PLAYGROUND SUBCOMMITTEE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA noted discussions are still being had on the location of the
  park. She explained that at a recent community meeting, one resident was opposed to
  the park due to horse interference but others representing small families stated reasons
  why the park would be beneficial. Community Services Supervisor Morquecho stated a
  survey would be brought to the Commission to gauge public interest and feedback.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  2
APRIL 19, 2021
   CHAIR POPE asked how the Equestrian Committee felt about the proposed park.
  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho stated they are open to the idea with
  suggestions of equipment like Butcher Park which stays low to the ground. Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith added that recent exercise groups working out in the area have
  not had a negative effect on the riders in the ring nearby.

  C.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  CHAIR POPE presented an email from COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asking for a
  Summer Concert event, describing that the event would be like the movie events with
  picnic blankets instead of cars and a ticketing system would work if numbers are a
  concern. This event could be a part of the Pepper Tree Foundation’s fund-raising events.
  CHAIR POPE noted the past Remember the Music Festival which was in the same
  category of event. COMMISSIONER ROMAELLI added well-placed speakers in the
  equestrian grass area which acted as a natural amphitheater for the past event.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted a similar event taking place in Palos Verdes
  Estates which used a cover band. Community Services Supervisor Morquecho suggested
  staff research the event further and bring its findings back to the Commission at a later
  date.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted partnering with the Remember the Music Foundation once
  more. COMMISSIONER BAIN asked why the City was no longer in partnership with the
  foundation. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted a conflict when the City ceased to pair
  the foundation’s event with the City Celebration event.

  CHAIR POPE added that the County also sponsors events such as these.
  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the Botanic Garden also hosts similar events and the City
  could consider forming a synergistic partnership with them.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated the library is hosting a Nature Book event on April 22 on
  California Native Plants sponsored by the Palos Verdes Land Conservancy. She
  suggested this Zoom activity could also be an event the City could sponsor to promote
  their own events and that cross-programming could be had with the Library and the Land
  Conservancy for future events.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  COVID-19 UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor stated that numbers are declining and basketball hoops
  are back at Ernie Howlett Park. She further shared that park reservations are back now
  that the County has moved to the Orange Tier allowing for gatherings of up to 100 people
  which will open up for horse shows as well as park permits at Ernie Howlett Park.

  B.  SPECIAL EVENTS UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho noted the drive-in movie held the previous
  Saturday was a success with 40 cars in attendance and Waste Management stepping in

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  3
APRIL 19, 2021
   as a sponsorship with a donation of $750 and goodie bags. The screen location may be
  adjusted for future viewings.

  The Mayor’s Ride will be postponed until June or July due to current COVID protocols.
  The Tracy Austin Subcommittee will meet on Wednesday to discuss the event as
  tournaments are still not allowed. Double’s play is now permitted allowed under the
  protocols and staff has applied for a waiver for the event.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MARCH 9, 2021

  Received and filed.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MARCH 23, 2021

  Received and filed.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  HIGHRIDGE PARK MURAL

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho noted that the artist Marianna will be meeting
  with the Commission in July during the Highridge Park Tour to follow up on the status of
  the mural.

  B.  JUNIOR LEAGUE SHED REPLACEMENT REQUEST

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho noted the current shed is deteriorating and
  a larger 8 feet by 10 feet shed will be requested by the League in May. Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith noted the location of the proposed larger shed would be the by
  the bullpen near first base. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if there were any
  requirements by the City that the Junior League could meet before they meet in May.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that suggestions were given to the
  Junior League but the proposed shed is a bit too large for the area. COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA noted that the location of the current shed is there to prevent players who
  are running to catch a foul ball from running into a shed.

  11.  PARK TOURS

  A.  GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER/PRESERVE AND DAPPLEGRAY PARK

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted some signs are currently being replaced at
  the site. Irrigation repairs have been made but were cut by someone later on. Missing
  trash and recycling containers were replaced. Drinking fountains were taken apart and
  disinfected for public use. He also noted that some residents dump tree debris in the area

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  4
APRIL 19, 2021
   which will be monitored by staff. He added that some sycamore trees are slated to be
  removed in the area as well.

  Dapplegray Park has removed trees that were encroaching onto the horse ring.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 7:02 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES MEETING ON MAY 17, 2021 AT 6:00 P.M., WHICH WILL MEET
  AT PEPPERWOOD PARK, CRENSHAW BLVD., ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  _____________________________
  Daniel A-Haja  Lisa Pope
  Community Services Coordinator  Park & Activities Commission, Chair

DRAFT PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  5
APRIL 19, 2021
